claims.text: At tag stage-0 the example repository has no application yet, and it contains the team's own note docs/team/sprint-example.md describing one past sprint.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: STAGE.md 'What exists at this tag'; docs/team/sprint-example.md

claims.text: In that note the two lines under the title state the length as two weeks and the team as one product owner, one scrum master, four developers and one tester.
In that note the sprint goal is one sentence: a customer can cancel an unpaid order without calling the call centre.

Its sprint backlog table lists five pieces of work with an owner, a number in the Uoc luong column and a final status; four are Xong and the fifth, stopping notifications for cancelled orders, is Chua xong, chuyen sprint sau.

Its daily example gives a junior three sentences (yesterday, today, blocked on whether a shipped order may be cancelled) and states the third is the most important; the daily is not a report to a manager but the team re-planning a day.

Its review section states the team demonstrates on a test environment rather than a personal machine, and that the unfinished piece is not demonstrated because unfinished does not count even when nearly all the code is written.

Its retrospective records one thing that worked (conditions written before coding), one that hurt (work only one person could do) and one action (anything with a number above three gets two people reading the code).

The reference description of Scrum names three accountabilities (product owner, scrum master, developers), which this lesson calls roles; five events (the sprint plus planning, daily, review, retrospective); and three artifacts (product backlog, sprint backlog, increment).
claims.source_hint: Scrum Guide 2020, sections 'Scrum Team', 'Scrum Events', 'Scrum Artifacts'

claims.text: In that reference the sprint is a fixed-length event of one month or less and contains the other four events; a new sprint starts as soon as the previous one ends. Cutting the work instead of moving the date is what fixed length implies, not a separate rule the reference states.

In that reference the product owner is accountable for what is built and its order, the developers for how the work is done and how much is taken in, and the scrum master for the way of working and removing impediments — not for managing the developers.

In that reference the increment must be usable and must meet the standard the team agreed in advance; work that does not meet it is not part of the increment, and more than one increment may be created within a sprint.

In that reference the daily belongs to the developers, lasts 15 minutes, is held at the same time every working day of the sprint, and exists to inspect progress toward the goal and re-plan the day's work; it is not a status report.

In that reference the review inspects the outcome of the sprint with key stakeholders and the product backlog may be adjusted as a result; the retrospective is about how the team works, and the team addresses the most impactful improvements as soon as possible. No number is prescribed.

The reference names no tester and no specialist roles at all: everyone doing the work is a developer, and it forbids sub-teams inside the team. It makes the developers responsible for sizing without naming a unit, so a number against each piece of work is one permitted way of sizing.
In a daily, the sentence worth saying is the one that changes somebody's plan for today — which is why this team's note marks the blocked sentence as the most important one.

An adaptation that keeps the fixed length, the single goal, the daily and the definition of finished leaves the parts listed in Core concepts in place; one that drops an event or stretches the date leaves a part out, which the reference says covers up problems and limits the benefits.
claims.source_hint: Scrum Guide 2020, section 'Scrum Definition', immutability paragraph

claims.text: When a team repeatedly extends its sprint, it has no date fixed in advance to measure against, so it cannot tell whether it is slow or the numbers in its estimate column are wrong.
Knowing the reference version of Scrum is what lets a junior tell a local adaptation that keeps its parts in place from one that leaves a part out.
In that reference the sprint review is a working session, and the team should avoid limiting it to a presentation.
The reference description of Scrum is a document called the Scrum Guide.

In the reference the product backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product; the sprint backlog is the sprint goal (why), the items selected (what) and an actionable plan for delivering the increment (how), a plan by and for the developers.

The reference states that implementing only parts of Scrum is possible but the result is then not Scrum; so a team dropping the fixed length has chosen a different way of working rather than a broken Scrum.
